title: Concept: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is not a bare origin
description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin contains a path or a trailing slash after the host. A browser compares the value against the requesting origin, which never carries a path, so the match fails and the response is denied to the site the operator meant to trust.
risk: Cross-origin access is denied for the intended site while the configuration looks correct; LOW severity because it is a functional break, not an exposure.
